def _timeout(config: IntegrationConfig) -> float:
    return float(getattr(config, "timeout", None) or 20.0)


def _json(response: requests.Response) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        data = response.json()
    except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        raise SearchBackendError(f"invalid JSON response (HTTP {response.status_code})")
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise SearchBackendError("unexpected response shape")

def _get(url, params=None, headers=None, timeout=20.0):
    try:
        response = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers, timeout=timeout)
    except requests.RequestException as ex:
        raise SearchBackendError(str(ex) or ex.__class__.__name__)
    if response.status_code >= 400:
        raise SearchBackendError(f"HTTP {response.status_code}")

"""SSRF, size and deadline guards for model driven web access.

``fetch_webpage`` is callable by an LLM, so the URL it receives is untrusted:
without explicit checks a prompt (or a poisoned page) can make the backend read
``http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data``, the Docker socket through a local
HTTP API or any service of the internal network.  This module is the only
place where outbound HTTP for the web tools is validated:

* scheme allow-list (``http`` / ``https`` only);
* DNS resolution plus private / reserved address rejection, re-checked on
  every redirect hop (a public URL must not bounce to ``127.0.0.1``);
* bounded body size and a wall-clock deadline;
* a small, honest set of request headers.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import ipaddress
import logging
import socket
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, List, Optional
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlsplit, urlunsplit

import requests

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Schemes accepted for outbound requests.
ALLOWED_SCHEMES = ("http", "https")

#: Maximum number of redirect hops followed before giving up.
MAX_REDIRECTS = 5

#: Size of the chunks read from the socket.
CHUNK_SIZE = 64 * 1024

#: Default body limit (3 MB is far more than any readable article).
DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES = 3 * 1024 * 1024

#: Default wall-clock budget for the whole request, redirects included.
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 15.0

#: Hostnames that never resolve to a legitimate public site.
BLOCKED_HOSTNAMES = frozenset({
    "localhost",
    "localhost.localdomain",
    "ip6-localhost",
    "metadata",
    "metadata.google.internal",
    "instance-data",
})

#: Suffixes that only exist inside a private network.
BLOCKED_HOST_SUFFIXES = (".localhost", ".local", ".internal", ".home.arpa")

#: Reserved IPv4 ranges: private, loopback, link-local (cloud metadata),
#: carrier grade NAT, documentation and multicast space.
_BLOCKED_V4 = tuple(
    ipaddress.ip_network(network)
    for network in (
        "0.0.0.0/8",

"""Reader-mode HTML to markdown extraction for the model facing web tools.

An LLM pays for every character it reads, so ``fetch_webpage`` never forwards a
raw page: navigation, menus, cookie banners, scripts and footers are removed
first and the remaining article is turned into markdown.

The extractor is a chain, in this order:

* ``trafilatura`` when it is installed (best boilerplate removal);
* a stdlib reader-mode fallback using ``html.parser`` so the tool keeps
  working on a bare installation and in the test suite.

``trafilatura`` output is validated against the page chrome that was found in
the raw document: when a navigation or footer token survives extraction the
result is discarded and the deterministic fallback is used instead.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import logging
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from typing import List, Optional

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Text below this length is not worth spending tokens on ("thin" page).
MIN_TEXT_CHARS = 200

#: A page whose readable text is a tiny fraction of its markup is thin too
#: (JavaScript shells, cookie walls, redirect stubs).
MIN_TEXT_RATIO = 0.05

#: Phrases that only appear on anti-bot interstitials. A page matching one of
#: them must be escalated to the browser instead of being read as content.
BOT_WALL_MARKERS = (
    "just a moment",
    "enable javascript and cookies to continue",
    "checking your browser",
    "verify you are human",
    "attention required",
    "cf-browser-verification",
    "access denied",
    "captcha",
)

#: Blocks that never carry article content.
CHROME_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(
    r"<(nav|footer|aside|header)\b[^>]*>(.*?)</\1>", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL
)

_TITLE_RE = re.compile(r"<title[^>]*>(.*?)</title>", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
_IMAGE_RE = re.compile(r"!\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\)")
_LINK_RE = re.compile(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)")
_EMPHASIS_RE = re.compile(r"[*_`~]+")
_HTML_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"<[^>]+>")
_SPACES_RE = re.compile(r"[ \t]+")
_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9]{6,}")


@dataclass
class ExtractedContent:

    Attributes:

    markdown: str = ""
    url: str = ""
    title: str = ""

    @property

        """The readable text without markdown syntax."""

"""Fetch pipeline of the model facing ``fetch_webpage`` tool.

:func:`fetch_page` is the single entry point, and the only place where the
pieces of the web stack are assembled:

1. :func:`codx.junior.web.guard.validate_url` rejects bad schemes and private /
   reserved targets before any socket is opened;
2. :func:`codx.junior.web.guard.safe_get` performs the bounded request (body
   size, wall-clock deadline, redirects re-validated on every hop);
3. :mod:`codx.junior.web.extract` turns the HTML into chrome free markdown;
4. when the page is a JavaScript shell, a cookie wall or an anti-bot
   interstitial and ``browser_escalation`` is enabled, ``browser_fetch`` renders
   it once with Chromium and the extraction is retried;
5. the markdown is capped to the requested number of characters, so the model
   never pays for content it did not ask for.

``validate_url`` and ``safe_get`` are module level names on purpose: tests
replace them to exercise the pipeline without network access.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

    bot_wall_reason,

        url: URL that was requested.
        final_url: URL after redirects.
        status: HTTP status of the last hop.
        title: Document title, when the page declares one.
        markdown: Chrome free article, already capped.
        extractor: Strategy that produced ``markdown`` (``trafilatura``,
            ``reader``, ``empty`` or ``pdf``).
        content_type: ``Content-Type`` of the response.
        rendered: True when Chromium had to render the page.
        truncated: True when the body or the markdown was cut.
        bytes_read: Body bytes read from the socket.
        wall_reason: Anti-bot marker that was detected, if any.
        note: Human readable remark about the result (empty when all went well).
        redirects: Redirect hops that were followed.
    """

    url: str
    final_url: str = ""
    status: int = 0
    title: str = ""
    markdown: str = ""
    extractor: str = ""
    content_type: str = ""
    rendered: bool = False
    truncated: bool = False
    bytes_read: int = 0
    wall_reason: Optional[str] = None
    note: str = ""
    redirects: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        """True when no readable text could be extracted."""
        return not (self.markdown or "").strip()


def _load_settings(settings: Optional[WebSettings]) -> WebSettings:
    """Return the given settings, or the project ones (never failing)."""
    if settings is not None:
        return settings
    try:
        return load_web_settings()
    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive, fetch must not break
        return WebSettings()


def _escalate(page: FetchedPage, settings: WebSettings) -> Optional[FetchedPage]:
    """Render ``page`` with Chromium, when the browser module is installed.

    Args:
        page: Page that came back as a JavaScript shell or a browser wall.
        settings: Resolved web settings (timeouts, private host policy).

    Returns:
        Optional[FetchedPage]: The rendered page, or ``None`` when escalation is
        unavailable or failed (the caller then returns the static extraction).
    """
    try:
        from . import browser_fetch
    except ImportError:
        logger.debug("browser escalation requested but browser_fetch is missing")
        return None

    renderer = getattr(browser_fetch, "render_page", None) or getattr(
        browser_fetch, "fetch_rendered", None
    )
    if renderer is None:
        logger.debug("browser_fetch exposes no renderer")
        return None

    try:
        return renderer(
            page.final_url or page.url,
            timeout=settings.timeout,
            allow_private=settings.allow_private_hosts,
        )
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - depends on Chromium
        logger.warning("browser escalation failed for %s: %s", page.url, ex)
        return None


def _limit_for(max_chars: Optional[int], settings: WebSettings) -> Optional[int]:
    """Resolve the markdown cap: explicit value first, settings as fallback."""
    if max_chars is None:
        return settings.max_output_chars
    try:
        value = int(max_chars)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return settings.max_output_chars
    return value if value > 0 else None


def fetch_page(
    url: str,
    max_chars: Optional[int] = None,
    settings: Optional[WebSettings] = None,
    allow_private: Optional[bool] = None,
    headers: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
) -> FetchResult:
    """Fetch a URL and return its readable content as markdown.

    Args:
        url: Target URL (untrusted, validated by the guard).
        max_chars: Cap for ``markdown``; defaults to
            ``settings.max_output_chars``. ``<= 0`` means no cap.
        settings: Resolved web settings; loaded from the project when omitted.
        allow_private: Override of ``settings.allow_private_hosts``.
        headers: Extra request headers merged over the guard defaults.

    Returns:
        FetchResult: Markdown, metadata and the diagnostics of the pipeline.

    Raises:
        UnsafeUrlError: The URL is unsafe, unresolvable or redirects too much.
        FetchError: The server answered with a 4xx/5xx status.

    Example:
        >>> fetch_page("https://example.com").markdown[:20]  # doctest: +SKIP
        'Example Domain'
    """
    resolved = _load_settings(settings)
    private_ok = resolved.allow_private_hosts if allow_private is None else bool(allow_private)

    target = validate_url(url, allow_private=private_ok)
    page = safe_get(
        target,
        headers=headers,
        timeout=resolved.timeout,
        max_bytes=resolved.max_bytes,
        allow_private=private_ok,
    )

    if is_pdf(page):
        return FetchResult(
            url=url,
            final_url=page.final_url or target,
            status=page.status,
            content_type=page.content_type,
            extractor="pdf",
            markdown="",
            bytes_read=page.bytes_read,
            truncated=page.truncated,
            note="PDF document: only the link is returned, no text is extracted",
            redirects=list(page.redirects),
        )

    html = page.text or ""
    content = extract_content(html, url=page.final_url or target)
    wall = bot_wall_reason(html)

    rendered = False
    note = ""
    if (
        resolved.browser_escalation
        and is_html(page)
        and (wall or content.is_empty or is_thin(content, html_len=len(html)))
    ):
        rendered_page = _escalate(page, resolved)
        if rendered_page is not None:
            page = rendered_page
            html = page.text or ""
            content = extract_content(html, url=page.final_url or target)
            wall = bot_wall_reason(html)
            rendered = True
        else:
            note = "the page looks like a browser wall and no browser is available"

    markdown = clean_markdown(content.markdown)
    markdown, cut = truncate_markdown(markdown, _limit_for(max_chars, resolved))

    return FetchResult(
        url=url,
        final_url=page.final_url or target,
        status=page.status,
        title=content.title or page.url,
        markdown=markdown,
        extractor=content.extractor,
        content_type=page.content_type,
        rendered=rendered,
        truncated=bool(cut or page.truncated),
        bytes_read=page.bytes_read,
        wall_reason=wall,
        note=note,
        redirects=list(page.redirects),
    )

"""Chromium escalation for JavaScript rendered pages.

The static pipeline (:mod:`codx.junior.web.guard` + :mod:`codx.junior.web.extract`)
is enough for server rendered pages, but a single page application answers with
an empty shell and a few ``<script>`` tags. :func:`render_page` takes over in
that case: it loads the URL in a headless Chromium (Playwright), waits for the
network to settle and returns the *rendered* DOM as a :class:`FetchedPage`, so
the caller keeps using exactly the same extraction path.

Playwright is an optional dependency (the ``browser`` extra of
``api/pyproject.toml``), and the browser runtime is not present in the slim
image. The module therefore imports it lazily: when it is missing
:class:`BrowserUnavailable` is raised, and
:func:`codx.junior.web.fetch._escalate` falls back to the static extraction
instead of failing the tool.

The session oriented automation lives in :mod:`codx.junior.browser` (containers,
CDP, audit); this module is deliberately stateless and session free, because the
``fetch_webpage`` tool must work without a shared computer session.
"""

import asyncio
import concurrent.futures
import logging
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

from .guard import (
    DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES,
    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
    FetchedPage,
    validate_url,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Wall-clock budget of a render, in seconds. Rendering is slower than a GET.
DEFAULT_RENDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30.0

#: Wait after ``load`` for pending XHR/fetch calls, in milliseconds.
NETWORK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000

#: Default viewport: a desktop size, so responsive sites serve their full layout.
DEFAULT_VIEWPORT = {"width": 1366, "height": 900}

#: Desktop user agent; some sites serve a degraded page to obvious headless UAs.
DEFAULT_USER_AGENT = (
    "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) "
    "Chrome/124.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"
)

#: Resource types dropped before rendering: they never carry readable text and
#: they are the bulk of the transfer on media heavy pages.
BLOCKED_RESOURCES = ("media", "font", "websocket")


class BrowserUnavailable(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when Playwright, or its Chromium build, is not installed."""


class RenderError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when Chromium could not load the page."""


def is_available() -> bool:
    """Return True when the Playwright client can be imported.

    The check is cheap and side effect free, so callers can decide whether
    escalation is worth attempting at all.

    Returns:
        bool: True when ``playwright.sync_api`` is importable.
    """
    try:
        import playwright.sync_api  # noqa: F401
    except Exception:
        return False
    return True


def _timeout_seconds(timeout: Optional[float]) -> float:
    """Resolve the render timeout, falling back to the module default."""
    try:
        value = float(timeout)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return DEFAULT_RENDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
    return value if value > 0 else DEFAULT_RENDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS


def _bound(text: str, max_bytes: Optional[int]) -> tuple:
    """Cut ``text`` to ``max_bytes`` UTF-8 bytes.

    Args:
        text: Rendered markup.
        max_bytes: Byte budget (``None`` or ``<= 0`` disables the cap).

    Returns:
        tuple: ``(text, truncated)`` with the same contract as
        :func:`codx.junior.web.guard.safe_get`.
    """
    try:
        limit = int(max_bytes)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        limit = DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES
    if limit <= 0:
        return text, False
    encoded = text.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if len(encoded) <= limit:
        return text, False
    cut = encoded[:limit].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    return cut, True


def _render_sync(
    url: str,
    timeout: float,
    allow_private: bool,
    max_bytes: Optional[int],
    user_agent: str,
) -> FetchedPage:
    """Render ``url`` with the synchronous Playwright API.

    This helper must run in a thread without a running event loop: the
    synchronous API refuses to start otherwise.

    Args:
        url: Already validated URL.
        timeout: Render budget in seconds.
        allow_private: Whether private hosts are acceptable.
        max_bytes: Markup budget in bytes.
        user_agent: User agent sent by the browser context.

    Returns:
        FetchedPage: The rendered page.

    Raises:
        BrowserUnavailable: Playwright or Chromium is missing.
        RenderError: Chromium could not load the page.
    """
    try:
        from playwright.sync_api import Error as PlaywrightError
        from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - depends on the installation
        raise BrowserUnavailable("playwright is not installed") from ex

    timeout_ms = int(timeout * 1000)
    try:
        with sync_playwright() as playwright:
            browser = playwright.chromium.launch(
                headless=True,
                args=[
                    "--no-sandbox",
                    "--disable-dev-shm-usage",
                    "--disable-gpu",
                ],
            )
            try:
                context = browser.new_context(
                    user_agent=user_agent,
                    viewport=DEFAULT_VIEWPORT,
                    ignore_https_errors=False,
                )
                page = context.new_page()
                page.route(
                    "**/*",
                    lambda route: (
                        route.abort()
                        if route.request.resource_type in BLOCKED_RESOURCES
                        else route.continue_()
                    ),
                )
                response = page.goto(
                    url, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=timeout_ms
                )
                try:
                    page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle", timeout=NETWORK_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS)
                except PlaywrightError:
                    # Long polling / analytics keep the network busy: the DOM we
                    # already have is good enough.
                    logger.debug("networkidle not reached for %s", url)
                html = page.content()
                final_url = page.url or url
                status = int(getattr(response, "status", 0) or 0)
                headers: Dict[str, Any] = getattr(response, "headers", {}) or {}
                try:
                    content_type = headers.get("content-type", "text/html") or "text/html"
                except AttributeError:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                    content_type = "text/html"
            finally:
                browser.close()
    except BrowserUnavailable:
        raise
    except PlaywrightError as ex:
        raise RenderError(f"chromium could not render {url}: {ex}") from ex

    # A client side redirect may land on an internal address: re-validate the
    # URL Chromium actually visited, exactly like the static pipeline does.
    validate_url(final_url, allow_private=allow_private)

    text, truncated = _bound(html, max_bytes)
    return FetchedPage(
        url=url,
        final_url=final_url,
        status=status,
        content_type=content_type,
        text=text,
        bytes_read=len(text.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")),
        truncated=truncated,
        redirects=[],
    )


def render_page(
    url: str,
    timeout: Optional[float] = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
    allow_private: bool = False,
    max_bytes: Optional[int] = DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES,
    user_agent: str = DEFAULT_USER_AGENT,
) -> FetchedPage:
    """Load ``url`` in headless Chromium and return the rendered DOM.

    Args:
        url: Page to render.
        timeout: Render budget in seconds (defaults to the static fetch budget).
        allow_private: Whether private hosts are acceptable. ``False`` keeps the
            SSRF policy of :mod:`codx.junior.web.guard`.
        max_bytes: Markup budget in bytes; the body is cut and ``truncated`` set.
        user_agent: User agent used by the browser context.

    Returns:
        FetchedPage: Rendered page, ready for
        :func:`codx.junior.web.extract.extract_content`.

    Raises:
        UnsafeUrlError: When the URL (or its final redirect target) is not
            acceptable for an outbound request.
        BrowserUnavailable: When Playwright or its Chromium build is missing.
        RenderError: When Chromium could not load the page.
    """
    validate_url(url, allow_private=allow_private)
    budget = _timeout_seconds(timeout)
    args = (url, budget, allow_private, max_bytes, user_agent)

    try:
        asyncio.get_running_loop()
    except RuntimeError:
        # No loop in this thread: the synchronous API is safe to use directly.
        return _render_sync(*args)

    # The tool layer is async: the synchronous Playwright API refuses to start
    # inside a running loop, so it gets a worker thread of its own.
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as pool:
        return pool.submit(_render_sync, *args).result()


#: Alias kept for callers (and older integrations) using the other name.
fetch_rendered = render_page

__all__ = [
    "BrowserUnavailable",
    "RenderError",
    "DEFAULT_RENDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS",
    "DEFAULT_USER_AGENT",
    "DEFAULT_VIEWPORT",
    "fetch_rendered",
    "is_available",
    "render_page",
]
